title: Relative coherent transfer for cellular enriched weighted cones
statement:
Use quasicategories and coherent parameters of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], complete algebroids of [def-coef-complete-algebroid], the enriched functor calculus of [lem-coef-enriched-category-tensor-calculus], and compatible enriched simplicial presentations of [lem-coef-enriched-simplicial-presentation]. Let $\mathcal V$ be a presentably closed symmetric monoidal infinity-category, $J$ a small simplicial category, and $F,G:J\to\mathscr P$ strict simplicial diagrams in such a presentation. A weight is a simplicial functor $W:J\to\mathsf{sSet}$. Call a weight cellular when it is built from the empty weight by small transfinite compositions of pushouts of coproducts of $J(j,-)\times\partial\Delta^n\to J(j,-)\times\Delta^n$, $n\geq0$; use the same definition starting at $R$ for a relative cellular inclusion $R\hookrightarrow W$.

Suppose enriched functors $h_j:E_{Fj}\to E_{Gj}$ have natural equivalences $G(\alpha)h_j\simeq h_kF(\alpha)$ for arrows $\alpha:j\to k$, with all composition, unit and higher simplicial compatibilities. This means a coherent transformation whose intertwiners are equivalences, rather than equalities of simplicial maps. A coherent map between two such transformations consists of enriched transformations of their components and coherent commutative intertwining squares, including their higher simplices; its components need not be equivalences. Then for a cellular $W$ these data induce an enriched functor between the categories of strict $W$-weighted cones on $F$ and $G$, and coherent maps induce enriched transformations. These categories are the enriched weighted limits when those are formed. The construction retains arbitrary small coherent parameter diagrams, their maps and higher simplices, and coherently respects composition and identities.

For a strict cone $b$, its transferred cone is connected to $h_jb_j$ by the specified coherent equivalences on all components and all cell restrictions. In particular it need not be the literal componentwise composite. These equivalences identify the coherent diagrams of mapping objects, including precomposition and postcomposition maps and every cell-attachment boundary map. Thus natural equivalences between such mapping-object diagrams can be checked on the corresponding unrectified component data.

The transfer has the following relative form. If $R\hookrightarrow W$ is relative cellular and a strict transferred $R$-cone is specified together with a coherent equivalence to the proposed component data on $R$, a strict transferred $W$-cone and a compatible equivalence can be chosen restricting to that $R$-cone. This assertion holds for enriched families of cones and transformations, not merely for their vertices. For a representable $R=J(j,-)$, fixing its cone means fixing its evaluation object; if $R\to W$ is bijective on vertices this fixes all object values forced by strict equivariance. Unit and associative comparisons and their coherence simplices are transferred by the same parameter assertion. None of these conclusions asserts that arbitrary chosen noninvertible intertwiners can replace the specified equivalences.

source.place: Agent-formulated relative enriched transfer lemma using the projective cell/cotensor calculus of sections 5.1--5.3 and the relative walking-module tower in Observation 6.2.4. This general coherent-transformation rectification assertion is a separate foundational obligation, not a theorem quoted verbatim from Riehl--Verity. Archival copy WANTED; no Stacks tag states it.

proof.text: Choose the compatible enriched simplicial presentation for the small family consisting of F, G, the h_j, and all specified intertwiners. The presentation represents every functor, transformation, and higher simplex and may be enlarged by the cotensors used by the cellular construction. Apply the flexible-weight enriched-lift theorem to F and to G: for a cellular W it constructs the complete enriched weighted-limit categories, identifies their underlying simplicial categories with strict W-cones, and retains all transformation simplices. Thus the strict cone categories used below are supplied by that theorem; they are not obtained merely by imposing equations in an unproved full subcategory.

source.place: Agent proof; flexible-weight construction and compatible presentation

proof.text: For the representable cell J(j,-), the flexible-weight theorem identifies the weighted construction with the cotensor/evaluation construction at F(j), and similarly at G(j). Apply h_j to the evaluation object and use the specified equivalences G(alpha)h_j ≃ h_kF(alpha), including their unit, composition, and higher simplicial compatibilities. The compatible presentation realizes these data on the entire simplicial set of representable cones. A coherent map of representable cones is sent to its component transformation together with every coherence simplex, so this is an enriched functor and preserves composition and identities at the representable stage.

Fix a complete $\mathcal V$-category $B$ as vertex. By the functor-category clause of the flexible-weight theorem, enriched functors $B\to\{W,G\}_J$ and their transformation simplices are the strict enriched $W$-cones with vertex $B$, whose $r$-simplices are natural maps $W\times\Delta^r\to Q_G(-)$, where $Q_G(j)=U\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathcal V}(B,G_j)$; likewise for $F$. The presentation realizes $Q_F,Q_G$ as strict simplicial diagrams and postcomposition with $h_j$ as strict maps $Q_F(j)\to Q_G(j)$, with the intertwiner simplices. Assume the transfer through a cellular stage $W_\alpha$ and attach a coproduct of cells $J(j,-)\times\partial\Delta^n\to J(j,-)\times\Delta^n$. By the theorem's pushout-to-pullback clause and the Yoneda lemma, extending a strict $W_\alpha$-cone $c$ over one cell means choosing an $n$-simplex $\sigma$ of $Q_G(j)$ with $\sigma|_{\partial\Delta^n}$ equal to the boundary prescribed by $c$. The $F$-cone gives an $n$-simplex $\tau$ of $Q_F(j)$, and $h_j\tau$ has boundary connected to the prescribed one by the already-constructed equivalence $e$. This $e$ is an edge of $\operatorname{Fun}(\partial\Delta^n,Q_G(j))$ whose vertex components are equivalences, hence an equivalence edge by the componentwise criterion for cotensors in the enriched tensor calculus. Restriction $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^n,Q_G(j))\to\operatorname{Fun}(\partial\Delta^n,Q_G(j))$ is an isofibration by the exponential-isofibration theorem (take $\mathcal C=Q_G(j)$, $\mathcal D=\Delta^0$). Lift the inverse of $e$ to an equivalence $h_j\tau\to\sigma$ whose boundary is exactly the prescribed boundary. Choose independently for each cell of the coproduct, since coproducts of cells give products. For $n=0$ the boundary is empty and $\sigma=h_j\tau$ may be taken. Data already defined on $W_\alpha$ are never changed. Applying this with $B=\{W,F\}_J$ to its evaluation cone gives a strict $W$-cone on $G$ with that vertex, hence an enriched functor $\{W,F\}_J\to\{W,G\}_J$. Its value on each object is the cone transferred with vertex $\mathbf 1$.

source.place: Agent proof; successor cell and uniform boundary lifting

proof.text: Higher simplices and maps are transferred in the same way, with the cells already transferred on their faces held fixed. For an $r$-simplex of cones whose faces are already transferred, the extension over a cell is a lift against the corner map for $\partial\Delta^n\subseteq\Delta^n$ and the restriction $p:\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^r,Q_G(j))\to\operatorname{Fun}(\partial\Delta^r,Q_G(j))$. Here $p$ is an isofibration by the exponential-isofibration theorem, so the corner map is an isofibration by the same theorem. The equivalence to be lifted is componentwise an equivalence, hence an equivalence edge by the componentwise criterion of the tensor calculus. A coherent map between two specified transformations $h\Rightarrow h'$ gives a coherent $W\times\Delta^1$-shaped datum from $h\circ\mathrm{ev}$ to $h'\circ\mathrm{ev}$ with vertex $\{W,F\}_J$. Its components need not be equivalences. Transferring it, with both ends already transferred, is the case $r=1$. By the functor-category clause of the flexible-weight theorem, the resulting $1$-simplex of strict $W$-cones is an enriched transformation between the transferred enriched functors. Degenerate simplices and $2$-simplices of composites are transferred by the same lifts. The lifted equivalences therefore identify the transfers of identities and composites with identities and composites, coherently. Hence the composition and identity clauses hold; strict equality is not claimed. The relative-cone-equivalence lemma is not needed, since no universal colimit condition is invoked.

source.place: Agent proof; coherence and naturality of the successor construction

proof.text: At a limit ordinal $\beta$, a continuous cellular presentation has $W_\beta=\operatorname{colim}_{\alpha<\beta}W_\alpha$. A natural map out of $W_\beta\times\Delta^r$ is therefore exactly a compatible family of natural maps out of the $W_\alpha\times\Delta^r$. Each successor choice restricts exactly to the data at earlier stages, because boundaries are held fixed. Hence the family glues to a strict $W_\beta$-cone, and the component equivalences, each living on a cell attached at some earlier stage, glue likewise. This is an ordinary transfinite recursion with choices at successor stages and unions at limit stages. No homotopy limit of a tower is needed, because the transferred data are strict and agree on restrictions. The flexible-weight theorem says that continuous composites give inverse limits, with mapping objects the corresponding limits; so the glued data are objects and simplices of $\{W_\beta,G\}_J$. By transfinite induction, the transfer exists for every small cellular $W$, including coproducts of cells at one stage. The transferred cone is connected to $h_jb_j$ by the lifted equivalences on every component and every cell restriction. The coherent-end and pullback formulas for mapping objects are functorial in their arguments through precomposition and postcomposition. These equivalences therefore identify the mapping-object diagrams of transferred cones with those of the unrectified component data, including every cell-boundary map.

source.place: Agent proof; limit stages and transfinite induction

proof.text: For a relative cellular inclusion $R\to W$, begin with the specified strict transferred $R$-cone and its specified coherent equivalence to the proposed component data, as the initial stage $W_0=R$. Then perform the successor construction of Step 3 and the gluing of Step 5 along a relative cellular presentation over $R$. At every cell, the lift has the boundary, including all $R$-data, held fixed exactly. Data on $R$ are therefore never changed, so the resulting $W$-cone restricts exactly to the given $R$-cone and its equivalence extends the given one. Running the construction with an arbitrary vertex $B$, and for $r$-simplices by the corner lifts of Step 4, gives the assertion for enriched families of cones and transformations with all parameter simplices. The flexible-weight functor-category clause identifies these families with enriched functors and transformations.

If R=J(j,-), the representable weighted-limit/cotensor description fixes the evaluation object at j. If R→W is bijective on vertices, strict equivariance fixes every object value forced by those vertices, and only higher cell simplices are extended. The unit and associative comparisons are among the specified coherence simplices and are transported by the same exponential boundary lifting. Finally, the flexible-weight theorem identifies the constructed strict cone categories, with all enriched transformations, with the enriched W-weighted limits whenever those limits are formed. This proves the two special clauses and the full relative assertion.

Small cases check out: a point with weight Δ^0 or Δ^1; J=[1] with weight J(0,-), where the result is equivalent to, not equal to, the literal composite; the empty weight; R=W. I found no duplicate (walking-module-weight-cells, enriched-coend-homotopy-invariance and pseudofunctor-split-family-strictification are different statements). The core argument is correct: equivalences lift with the boundary held fixed along the isofibrations Fun(Δ^n,Q)→Fun(∂Δ^n,Q) and the corner map (Kerodon 01F1/01F3). Three repairable faults are fixed in fixes/dag/nodes/sec-six-functors/lem-coef-cellular-weight-coherent-transfer.json. (a) Steps 3, 4 and 6 lifted only in UG_j (vertex 1), so the enriched functor and enriched families were not obtained. They now work in U Fun_V(B,G_j) for any vertex B; taking B={W,F}_J with its evaluation cone gives the enriched functor through the flexible-weight functor-category clause, and coherent maps are the r=1 corner lift with both ends held fixed. (b) C1/C4: the componentwise equivalence criterion was used without citation; lem-coef-enriched-category-tensor-calculus is now in the uses of Steps 3, 4 and 6 (no cycle).
